initial.base:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE standalone pixel-art dog style proposal for the nana project, square canvas.
Input roles: images 1 and 2 are STYLE references ONLY, image 3 is the actual dog's IDENTITY reference. The dog must be gray and white from photo 3, never brown/beagle from style refs.
Subject invariants: rounded short gray floppy ears at cheek sides, gray outer face, white central forehead blaze merging into white nose bridge and fluffy white muzzle/beard, gray back/body, white chest and paws, black nose. Modestly fluffy face and feet, shorter body coat. Do not invent a breed or change to long spaniel ears. Preserve this individual dog's recognizable gray-white layout. Tail may rest low beside haunch, dark gray feathery, no erect white-tipped beagle tail. Small dark eyes.
Composition invariant for comparison: ONE whole dog sitting in gentle front three-quarter view, facing slightly left but face toward viewer, both front paws visible, tail low to viewer right; head about 40% of full seated height, dog about 72% canvas height, generous uncluttered pale cream background. Gentle open mouth with tiny muted pink tongue. No props, collar, UI, text, labels, borders or additional views. Same simple seated pose across variants; this is a style proposal, not a production sprite.

variants.detail: STYLE A — soft shaded storybook pixel art, drawing primarily on reference 1. Fine clearly stair-stepped pixel contour, dark warm charcoal rather than pure black, delicate medium-fine pixel clusters, 4 restrained gray tonal planes giving rounded volume, subtle cream highlights, minimal pixelated grounding shadow. Friendly natural proportions, readable short tufts and fuller white beard. Crisp enlarged pixel edges, cozy 16-bit game illustration. Not crayon, no smooth vector lines, no photorealism, no blur, no noisy dithering. Richest and finest detail of the three proposals, but economical.

STYLE B — bold outlined graphic pixel character, drawing primarily on reference 2. Large obvious square-pixel staircase silhouette with thick near-black outline, flat gray and ivory blocks, a single muted lavender-gray shadow plane, small expressive dark pixel eyes with at most one tiny catchlight. Broad simplified white beard, ears and feet. Punchy cute readable silhouette, medium-coarse pixel grid, limited approximately 8-color look. No orange fur or colored cheeks; retain gray-white individual. No smooth curves, no airbrushing, no gradients, no elaborate fur texture. Strongest contour of the three proposals.

STYLE C — minimal compact game sprite, a restrained synthesis of both reference images. Visibly COARSE large square pixels, blocky economical shapes as if a carefully drawn roughly 40–48-pixel-tall sprite enlarged with nearest neighbor. Very sparse interior detail, small black dot-block eyes without sparkles, only 5–6 gray/ivory/charcoal/pink colors, selective thin dark contour on outer silhouette, avoid thick continuous black internal outline. Small white forehead blaze, broad white beard and chest must stay recognizable despite simplification. Friendly same pose and body proportions, no extreme giant head. No texture, no gradients, no smooth vector contours, no micro-pixels. Simplest and coarsest of the three.

Short broad floppy ears not spaniel; white central forehead blaze joins broad white beard. Gray torso, white bib and lower paws; completely dark gray short-feathered LOW tail with no white tip. Same seated front-three-quarter pose. Strong radically reduced chunky sprite design, not simply a photo pixel filter. Keep it charming and immediately legible, reduce shapes decisively. Uniform crisp rectangular pixel lattice edges. No gradients or paper texture, no smooth vector curves.

simplification.common:
Edit this specific pixel-art dog illustration following the user's correction: simplify fur MUCH MORE. Preserve seated pose, overall body proportions, canvas, cream background, dog size and the identity of the gray-white dog. Preserve the central white forehead blaze continuous with muzzle, gray cheeks/ears, white beard/chest/feet, low gray tail. No new spots or invented markings.
REMOVE ALL interior fur strokes, narrow streaks, little highlight islands, flecks, stippling, curls, layered zigzag hair bands and mosaic noise. Use large uninterrupted flat color areas. Describe fluffy fur ONLY through two or three broad modest notches along outer cheeks and feet, not a serrated outline. White beard is a simple rounded block shape, not many locks of hair. Ears are broad smooth floppy shapes with no interior fur lines. Body is an unbroken gray mass rather than individually shaded hairs. Keep small black eyes, black nose, tiny pink tongue and mouth readable. Do not add accessories or text. Preserve genuine stair-stepped pixel styling; do not turn into smooth vector artwork. Major flat coat regions are essential, reduce texture by at least 85%.

edits.style: Keep A's finer pixel scale, thin warm-dark outer contour and soft rounded volume, but render that volume using ONLY THREE large flat tonal areas per gray or white region. No hair texture. A is the softly shaded option.

Keep B's bold black pixel outline and medium chunky blocks. Each gray or white region gets a flat base and ONE broad clean shadow only. B is the bold graphic option. Remove the invented bright white tail tip: tail entirely gray.

Keep C's coarse square pixels and simple black square eyes with no glint. Almost flat fill; one solid gray shape for body, one solid gray for each ear, one white bib and one white beard. At most one small broad shadow under chin. C is the most minimal sprite option.
